newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles council orders arena disclosures-paper.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles council orders arena disclosures-paper.

text.p: The Los Angeles city council has ordered developers of a planned downtown sports complex to make public their lease agreement with the Lakers basketball team, according to a published report on Wednesday.
The documents were not immediately released, and it was unclear how much information would be made public by the developers, the Los Angeles Times reported.

Deputy City Attorney Patricia Tubert, who has seen the lease, said the agreement does not require the Lakers to play for a quarter-century in the proposed arena as previously promised, according to the Times.

In May, the city council approved plans to build a $200-million-plus sports and entertainment complex in downtown Los Angeles. Under the proposal, the city would contribute about $70 million to the project through the sale of bonds.
